bull_bear.body:
- Sustained audience leadership - TV Today Network retained its position as the No. 1 network of national news channels, with Aaj Tak leading the Hindi news genre through FY 2025-26 and Aaj Tak HD the No. 1 HD news channel
- Brand and editorial franchise - the Board's Report attributes performance to its brands, content, impeccable reputation and the sustained leadership of Aaj Tak, Aaj Tak HD and India Today, plus an extensive distribution network
- Unmatched digital reach - properties generated ~100 billion social media views and 2.3 billion engagements in FY26, with a collective subscriber/follower base of 452 million (50+ million added during the year), described as India's No. 1 media network by social media engagement
- Connected TV leadership - 10.5 billion CTV watch minutes, nearly 27% ahead of the closest competitor, and the highest monthly average watch time per viewer
- Multi-brand digital portfolio - 28 dedicated digital-first brands spanning regional, vertical and youth audiences, giving breadth beyond the linear TV channels
- Event-driven pull - No. 1 across all four days of Operation Sindoor and No. 1 TV channel across all genres during Bihar election counting hours, evidencing consistent draw in both scheduled and breaking news
- Global editorial access - world-exclusive interviews with heads of state and senior global figures that drew record concurrent viewership
- Editorial governance - stated mission of upholding the gold standard of journalism by de-linking editorial from business
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Advertising revenue concentration — The Board's Report states that a large part of the Company's revenue continues to come from advertising, so demand is tied to advertiser spending rather than a diversified revenue base.
- Strategic and market risk — A market slowdown and reduced marketing spend by key industry players may lead to reduced advertising demand and may impact revenue growth; mitigated by reviewing strategic decisions and market trends, diversifying investment across multiple growth opportunities and pursuing new avenues and business deals.
- Competition risk — Success of the news channels depends highly on viewership, brand position and the ability to innovate; with the emergence of new entrants, competition is described as a sustained risk. Mitigation rests on accurate and timely news delivery, brand investment, presence across all major Hindi-speaking markets and monitoring of viewership trends.
- Technology and innovation risk (AI-driven, platform-centric media) — BRSR flags obsolescence of traditional workflows and formats from rapid adoption of AI-enabled production, overdependence on a few third-party platforms and algorithms affecting visibility, distribution control and monetisation stability, and capability gaps in adopting AI, automation and advanced analytics. Mitigated through intelligent automation, strengthening owned-and-operated platforms, and upskilling in AI and data.
- Cybersecurity and data privacy — Risk of financial loss or disruption of operations from failure of IT systems, hackers gaining access to the website/platforms or sensitive data, and virus/malware/ransomware attacks; a data-security lapse could impact stakeholder trust, disrupt operations and cause regulatory or reputational consequences. Mitigated by ISO 27001 certification, Zero Trust architecture, encryption, backups, periodic vulnerability assessments, multiple security controls and a cyber insurance policy.
- Regulatory, compliance and litigation risk — Any default may attract penal provisions and impact the Company's reputation, and the Company may face litigation from third parties by virtue of being in the news industry. Mitigated through a compliance monitoring system, in-house legal experts and external consultation, and continuous monitoring of regulatory changes.
- Health, safety and employee well-being — BRSR material-issue table records that the fast-paced nature of the media industry exposes the workforce to significant health and safety risks, with negative financial implications; mitigated by group insurance, an in-house medical facility, hospital partnerships, wellness workshops and PPE.
- Loss of assets or profit due to natural calamities and operational concentration — Climate change may increase the frequency and severity of natural disasters, and companies with major/key operations concentrated at one place are at risk; mitigated by analysing disaster impact, planning protective measures and maintaining adequate insurance coverage.
- Ethical governance and compliance — Identified as a material risk in BRSR - any instance of non-compliance can significantly affect business operations, brand reputation and overall credibility; mitigated through tone at the top, a defined Code of Conduct, a Risk Management Committee, an enterprise risk management framework and an online compliance management system.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: T.V. Today Network Limited is an India-based company in the media and entertainment industry, operating mainly in television broadcasting and other media operations. It runs four TV news channels - Aaj Tak, Aaj Tak HD, India Today TV and Good News Today - alongside 28 dedicated digital-first brands, and broadcasts news and current affairs across multiple platforms including television and digital media. Its major customers are advertisers (private, public, government and other entities advertising on its platforms) and viewers/subscribers of its channels and digital platforms.

business.body:
- Sustained audience leadership - TV Today Network retained its position as the No. 1 network of national news channels, with Aaj Tak leading the Hindi news genre through FY 2025-26 and Aaj Tak HD the No. 1 HD news channel
- Brand and editorial franchise - the Board's Report attributes performance to its brands, content, impeccable reputation and the sustained leadership of Aaj Tak, Aaj Tak HD and India Today, plus an extensive distribution network
- Unmatched digital reach - properties generated ~100 billion social media views and 2.3 billion engagements in FY26, with a collective subscriber/follower base of 452 million (50+ million added during the year), described as India's No. 1 media network by social media engagement
- Connected TV leadership - 10.5 billion CTV watch minutes, nearly 27% ahead of the closest competitor, and the highest monthly average watch time per viewer
- Multi-brand digital portfolio - 28 dedicated digital-first brands spanning regional, vertical and youth audiences, giving breadth beyond the linear TV channels
- Event-driven pull - No. 1 across all four days of Operation Sindoor and No. 1 TV channel across all genres during Bihar election counting hours, evidencing consistent draw in both scheduled and breaking news
- Global editorial access - world-exclusive interviews with heads of state and senior global figures that drew record concurrent viewership
- Editorial governance - stated mission of upholding the gold standard of journalism by de-linking editorial from business
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Strengthen leadership across platforms, deploy technology responsibly and maintain editorial integrity, while deepening direct engagement with audiences and reducing dependence on third-party algorithms (Chairman's 'The Road Ahead')
- Build trusted, brand-safe environments valued by both consumers and advertisers, on the view that trust - not technology - is the defining challenge for media
- Human-centric AI transformation: deploy AI to enhance speed, scale and relevance across the newsroom while keeping accuracy, depth and editorial integrity central; technology empowers journalists but never replaces them
- Lead the industry's AI transformation from the front - launched Sutra, an AI-powered multilingual news anchor developed with BharatGen, and served as Official AI Partner of WAVES 2025
- Digital-first strategy to cement position as India's leading digital news powerhouse across digital, social media and connected TV ecosystems
- Early conviction in Connected TV as the new frontier of audience engagement, positioning the Group to lead the reinvention of television for the digital age
- Continued bold investment in next-generation products - scaling MO (Gen Z platform), launching vPaper (video-enabled ePaper) and Health Wealth - to diversify content formats and enrich the digital ecosystem
- Sustain category leadership in digital audio/podcasts (Teen Taal, Storybox, Padhaku Nitin, In Our Defence), extending flagship shows beyond digital into live shows and community meet-ups
- Divest the Radio Business (three FM stations in Mumbai, Delhi and Kolkata under 104.8 FM) as a going concern through wholly owned subsidiary Vibgyor Broadcasting Private Limited, in order to focus on the Company's core business
- Retain earnings for future strategic requirements - the Board decided not to recommend any final dividend for FY 2025-26 and transferred no amount to the General Reserve
- The Company has a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy which determines the distribution of dividends in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws; the policy is published on the Company's website. The routed governance text sets out the policy framework only and does not state a payout intent or quantum.
- Materiality assessment covering employees, suppliers, distributors, customers and viewers, shareholders and community members identified seven key material topics aligned to the UN SDGs; the high-priority set is Ethical Governance and Compliance, Health Safety and Employee Well-being, Energy Management, Diversity Equity and Inclusion, Social Outreach, Technology and Innovation, and Data Privacy and Cyber Security
- Energy management treated as a strategic opportunity - disciplined electricity-usage efficiency to drive long-term cost efficiency, reduce exposure to energy-related risks and align operations with global sustainability goals
- Data privacy and cyber security programme: Information Security Policy aligned with ISO 27001 standards, executive oversight of cyber security as a strategic business risk, Zero Trust architecture, data encryption for critical/sensitive data, backups, continuous monitoring, access controls and periodic security assessments of the IT network
- Diversity, equity and inclusion positioned as an opportunity to strengthen workforce capability and make reporting more representative and credible across the country
- Employee well-being programme: group insurance coverage, an in-house medical facility at the corporate office staffed with qualified doctors and nurses, hospital partnerships for medical emergencies, workshops on physical fitness, mental well-being, social skills and emotional intelligence, and PPE kits where required
- Enterprise Risk Management framework with a Risk Management Committee comprising primarily directors, supported by a Board-approved Risk Management Policy covering risk identification, assessment and treatment and defining the risk organisation structure
- Two-tier stakeholder grievance redressal mechanism published on the Company's website, with dedicated communication channels for suppliers shared at vendor onboarding
- Social outreach and community engagement treated as an opportunity to contribute beyond broadcasting; CSR is applicable to the Company under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: TV Today's asset base is broadcast infrastructure rather than plant: during FY 2025-26 its production network comprised 13 studio and production facilities across four locations, supported by four virtual studio set-ups and 21 office facilities, with 100% broadcast uptime maintained across all channels. As part of a modernization initiative the Company developed a virtual studio with integrated audience participation powered by advanced AR and VR technologies, accommodating around 150 audience members, which serves as the primary venue for its flagship debate and discussion programmes. Its IT and digital infrastructure capital expenditure amounted to Rs 12.76 crore during FY 2025-26, including investments in AI-enabled technologies, and bandwidth capacity was expanded by 50% during the year. Technology upgrades, a new set-top box and the renewal of the satellite capacity agreement lowered annualised satellite transmission operating expenses substantially, while advanced modulation standards reduced bandwidth allocation at higher effective bit rates. Cybersecurity spend went into advanced endpoint protection, Next-Generation Firewalls and a Privileged Access Management solution, with the security framework aligned to ISO 27001:2022. Capital deployment priorities are stated as expanding the digital ecosystem and audience engagement capabilities while rationalising participation in genres that may not be financially viable in future, differentiating content across television, digital and emerging platforms, using data/technology/analytics for audience insight and monetisation efficiency, automating workflows, and developing new avenues of growth and revenue diversification. Looking ahead, management says the immediate priority is to restore operating momentum while retaining financial discipline, with costs, liquidity and capital deployment kept under close review, and investment remaining focused on digital platforms, content innovation, technology-enabled monetisation, automation and analytics; the infrastructure roadmap centres on deeper AI integration and modernisation (the routed text is truncated at this point).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's M&E sector grew to approximately Rs 2.78 lakh crore ($32 billion), outpacing nominal per capita GDP growth, and is in a digital-first reordering of how content is created, distributed and monetised
- Total advertising spends grew 13.5 per cent to around Rs 1.5 lakh crore, with digital media now accounting for 63 per cent of revenue and expanding roughly 30 per cent over the year
- The reach of online news platforms fell 9 per cent to 428 million as AI-generated search summaries and standalone AI applications began to reshape how audiences discover information - a structural pressure on digital news reach
- Television news viewership declined only 3 per cent despite the absence of a general election; Hindi news grew 4 per cent and English news 6 per cent while regional news softened; linear TV weekly reach held steady at around 745 million
- In March 2026 the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting directed the suspension of television rating points for all news channels, a measure subsequently extended - the Company continues to engage constructively with regulators
- Management attributes FY26 resilience to strong growth in digital revenue, disciplined cost management and continued investment in content innovation and platform diversification
- Real GDP growth estimated at 7.6 per cent for FY 2025-26, with contained inflation and healthy foreign exchange reserves supporting the demand backdrop
